scope_note: The historical 790-compound lockbox has already been examined. Every lockbox result produced here is retrospective validation, never prospective confirmation, and is excluded from model/hyperparameter selection.

selection_order: earliest candidate in the declared grid
shared.lockbox_policy: Select hyperparameters and refit duration using development folds only, refit on all development data, then score lockbox once per frozen development-selected model.

experiment_a_capacity.question: How much nonlinear readout capacity is needed to expose PXR signal in frozen Nesso representations?
experiment_a_capacity.primary_representation: elementwise mean of the two frozen 384D affinity representations

ridge.scaling: StandardScaler fit on each training partition

mlp_training.outer_refit_epochs: rounded median inner best epoch for the selected candidate; minimum 1
mlp_training.scaling: feature mean/SD fit only on the applicable training partition

primary_comparisons: mean384 one-hidden MLP minus mean384 ridge
mean384 two-hidden MLP minus mean384 ridge
mean384 two-hidden MLP minus mean384 one-hidden MLP
each mean384 probe minus the published pretrained twin-head fine-tune
experiment_a_capacity.seed_variability: Report each outer-refit seed separately plus the three-seed mean prediction.

experiment_b_standardization.question: Could chemical form handling or near-analogue leakage make the historical chemical split optimistic, and do conclusions survive a standardized split?
experiment_b_standardization.primary_standardization: RDKit MolStandardize Cleanup followed by FragmentParent; formal charge is retained rather than neutralized.
sensitivity_schemes: first InChIKey block from the primary fragment parent (connectivity sensitivity)

split.additional_union: Bemis-Murcko scaffold group; acyclic molecules use full primary standardized SMILES
split.assignment: largest component first, seeded random tie order and assignment to a currently smallest fold

split_audit.historical_alignment: Hungarian relabeling maximizes row overlap solely for reporting assignment changes; modeling uses the original deterministic standardized fold labels.

models.frozen_nesso_ridge: mean384 representation with alphas [0,1,10,100,1000], selected inside each outer training partition
models.lightgbm: published reduced 2D feature table and historical nested feature-selection/stopping recipe, but with the standardized chemical-family folds; those descriptor inputs remain based on the original prepared structures

experiment_b_standardization.interpretation: Fold-level metric changes across historical and standardized assignments are not ordinary row-paired model deltas. Overall OOF metrics reuse the same rows but arise from different training sets.

experiment_c_loss_lr.question: Was the historical learning-rate boundary or Huber delta=0.5 responsible for optimization behavior and high-end compression?
experiment_c_loss_lr.architecture: Released pretrained twin Nesso heads, each 384->384->384->1 with ReLU, initialized from the pinned checkpoint.
experiment_c_loss_lr.target_coordinate: 6-pEC50, matching the released head; exactly equivalent to direct pEC50 after sign/offset transformation of the final layer.

training.outer_refit_epochs: rounded median inner best epoch; minimum 1

experiment_c_loss_lr.nested_outputs: For every objective, select LR inside each outer training partition and produce three-seed outer OOF predictions. Also report an all-objective global selector as secondary.
primary_comparisons: each development-selected objective minus nested Huber delta=0.5
globally selected objective/LR minus published historical fine-tuned head
experiment_c_loss_lr.loss_scale_note: Native validation losses are compared across learning rates within an objective; MAE is used across different objective families because MSE, MAE, and Huber have different numerical scales.
